problems.title: An inverse function needs one-to-one behaviour
problems.question: Which listed function has an inverse on [0,π]?
problems.idea: A strictly monotone function is one-to-one.
formulas: sin(x/2) increases strictly from 0 to 1 on [0,π].
steps: Thus f(x)=1−sin(x/2) decreases strictly and has an inverse.
The other listed sine or squared-cosine functions repeat values on this interval.

problems.title: Products of shifted sines
problems.question: Evaluate sin(125°+α)sin(65°+α)−sin(145°−α)sin(25°−α).
problems.idea: Turn both products into cosine differences.
steps: The expression becomes [cos60°−cos(190°+2α)−cos120°+cos(170°−2α)]/2.
The last two angle-dependent cosines are equal, because both are −cos(10°+2α).
The result is [1/2−(−1/2)]/2.

problems.title: An equilateral triangle on a circle
problems.question: A=(√2,√2), B=(2cos75°,−2sin75°), C=(m,2sin165°) are equilateral-triangle vertices. Find m.
problems.idea: A and B lie on the radius-2 circle at angles 45° and −75°, separated by 120°.
formulas: The third angle is 165° for the equilateral triangle centred at the origin.
steps: The corresponding third vertex is (2cos165°,2sin165°).
The other equilateral completion has a different y-coordinate, so it does not satisfy the stated C-coordinate.
Thus m=2cos165°=−2sin75°.

problems.title: Signed distances of a centroid from a plane
problems.question: The distances of A,B,C from a plane are 9,12,15. Which listed distance cannot be the distance of their centroid from the plane?
problems.idea: The signed distance to a plane is an affine function.
formulas: Centroid signed distance=(signed dA+signed dB+signed dC)/3.
steps: Taking absolute values of all possible sign sums gives {12,6,4,2}.
For example all on one side gives 12; reversing the 9,12,15 signs individually gives 6,4,2.
The listed value 13 is impossible.

problems.title: Distance from a cube edge midpoint to a space diagonal
problems.question: A cube has edge √6. Find the distance from an edge midpoint to the nearest space diagonal.
problems.idea: Use the diagonal through one endpoint of that edge.
formulas: For a cube edge a, M=(a/2,0,0) and diagonal direction u=(1,1,1); distance²=|M|²−(M·u)²/|u|².
steps: The squared distance is a²/4−a²/12=a²/6.
With a=√6, the distance is 1. The other diagonal types are no closer by cube symmetry or the same projection calculation.

problems.title: Find a least period of π
problems.question: Which listed function has least positive period π?
problems.idea: Compare standard periods, including absolute values.
formulas: tan x has period π; |tan x| still has least period π.
steps: The other choices have periods 2π,4π,π/2,or π/10 as appropriate.
For example |sin10x| has least period π/10, while tan2x has period π/2.

problems.title: A minimum that is only an infimum
problems.question: E lies on the hypotenuse AB of a nondegenerate right triangle, with AE=3, EB=4. Find the smallest possible sum of distances from E to the legs.
problems.idea: Express those distances using the leg lengths.
steps: The sum is (3v+4u)/7, with u,v>0.
It exceeds 3: 3v+4u>3(v+u)>3√(u²+v²)=21.
As u tends to 0 and v tends to 7, the sum tends to 3. But u=0 would make the triangle degenerate.
problems.answer: There is no attained minimum; the infimum is 3.
problems.note: The printed answer 3 is a limiting value, not a possible minimum for a nondegenerate triangle.

problems.title: A negative principal arccos value is impossible
problems.question: Solve arccos x=−arccos(1/3).
problems.idea: The left side cannot be negative.
steps: The right side is strictly negative. Therefore equality cannot hold for any real x in the domain.

problems.title: Equal oblique segments give a cyclic quadrilateral
problems.question: Four equal oblique segments run from a point to a plane. What must be true of their four endpoints in the plane?
problems.idea: All four projections have the same length.
formulas: If H is the perpendicular foot and the common oblique length is L, each endpoint X satisfies HX²=L²−h².
steps: Thus all four endpoints lie on one circle centred at H.
They therefore form a cyclic quadrilateral, without a required parallelogram or rhombus shape.
problems.answer: A quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.

problems.title: Equal lateral areas do not determine an oblique prism’s base
problems.question: An oblique prism has equal-area lateral faces. Which listed base shape is necessarily forced?
problems.idea: Equal lateral areas constrain edge projections perpendicular to the lateral edges. They do not fix the base shape.
formulas: With lateral-edge vector v=(0,0,1), a face area equals the length of the base edge’s projection onto the xy-plane.
steps: Take base vertices A=(0,0,0),B=(1,0,1),C=(1/2,√3/2,1/2) in plane z=x.
Their xy projections form an equilateral triangle of side 1, so all three lateral face areas are 1.
The actual base sides are √2,√5/2,√5/2, so the base is not equilateral and is not any of the listed quadrilaterals. The prism is oblique.
problems.answer: None of the listed base shapes is guaranteed.
problems.note: The stated equal-area condition is insufficient to conclude that the base is a rhombus or any other listed shape.

problems.title: A rational trig equation with excluded inputs
problems.question: Solve sin x/(1+cos x)=1−cos x.
problems.idea: Keep 1+cos x≠0 when clearing the denominator.
steps: sin x(1−sin x)=0, so sin x=0 or 1.
From sin x=0, retain only x=2kπ because odd multiples of π make the denominator zero.
sin x=1 gives x=π/2+2kπ, all valid.

problems.title: Smallest positive root of a scaled sine equation
problems.question: Find the smallest positive solution of $\sin(\pi(2x-3)/6)=-1/2$.
problems.idea: Use the two standard sine branches.
steps: The first branch gives x=1+6k; the second x=5+6k.
The least positive member of their union is 1.

problems.title: Factor out a sum of sine and cosine
problems.question: Solve 3(cos x+sin x)=1+cos2x+sin2x.
problems.idea: Factor the right side.
formulas: 1+cos2x+sin2x=2cos²x+2sin x cos x=2cos x(cos x+sin x).
steps: The equation becomes (cos x+sin x)(3−2cos x)=0.
The second factor is at least 1, so cos x+sin x=0.

problems.title: Lateral area from a diagonal section of a box
problems.question: A rectangular box has diagonal-section area 4√6. The angle between its base diagonals is 30°. Find its lateral area.
problems.idea: Use the base-diagonal length d and height h.
steps: The angle condition gives ab=d²/4.
Then (a+b)²=d²+2ab=3d²/2, so a+b=d√(3/2).
Lateral area=2(a+b)h=2dh√(3/2)=24.

problems.title: A pyramid apothem equal to the base circumradius
problems.question: A regular triangular pyramid has apothem equal to the circumradius of its equilateral base. Find lateral area divided by base area.
problems.idea: Compare the two area formulas using a common perimeter.
formulas: Lateral area=Pl/2; base area=Pr/2; equilateral circumradius R=2r.
steps: Since l=R=2r, the ratio is l/r=2.

problems.title: Count two families of trig roots
problems.question: How many roots of $\sqrt2\sin10x+\sin2x=\cos2x$ lie in $[0,\pi]$?
problems.idea: Rewrite the right-side difference as a sine.
steps: The sine branches give x=π/48+kπ/6 and x=3π/32+kπ/4.
The first family has k=0,…,5 in the interval, giving 6 roots. The second has k=0,…,3, giving 4.
They cannot overlap: equating the formulas gives 16k−24l=7, impossible for integers.

problems.title: Count rational terms with prime exponents
problems.question: How many rational terms occur in $(\sqrt[4]{12}+1/\sqrt3)^{199}$?
problems.idea: A term is rational exactly when both prime exponents are integers.
steps: The exponent of 3 is integral when 199−3k is divisible by 4, or k≡1 (mod4).
These k are odd, so the exponent of 2 is also integral.
The allowed indices are 1,5,…,197: (197−1)/4+1=50.

problems.title: Two expansions with incompatible radical types
problems.question: How many common terms do the expansions of $(\sqrt2+\sqrt3)^7$ and $(\sqrt6+1)^6$ have?
problems.idea: Classify each nonzero term by its radical factor.
formulas: In the first expansion every term is a rational multiple of √2 or √3; in the second it is rational or a rational multiple of √6.
steps: The first exponent total is odd, so exactly one of the 2 and 3 prime exponents is half-integral.
The second expansion has either both prime exponents integral or both half-integral.
No nonzero term can belong to both types, regardless of its binomial coefficient.

problems.title: Rotate a point about another point
problems.question: Rotate A=(2,5) counterclockwise 90° about B=(1,−1). Find its image.
problems.idea: Translate to B, rotate, then translate back.
formulas: A−B=(1,6); a 90° counterclockwise rotation maps (u,v) to (−v,u).
steps: The rotated displacement is (−6,1).
Add B to get (−5,0).

problems.title: A linear maximum on a wedge
problems.question: Maximize x+2y if 2x−2≤y≤x+2.
problems.idea: Use the upper bound for y and the compatibility of both bounds.
steps: Thus the objective is at most 3·4+4=16.
At x=4, y=6 both bounds coincide and the value is 16.

problems.title: The fifth draw has the original colour proportion
problems.question: A box has 10 green and 15 blue balls. Five balls are drawn without replacement. Find the probability the fifth is green.
problems.idea: Every original ball is equally likely to occupy the fifth position.
formulas: P(green in any fixed draw position)=10/25.
steps: No conditioning on earlier colours is given, so the marginal probability is unchanged.

problems.title: Rain on ten days with no odd-numbered rainy date
problems.question: Assume exactly 10 rainy days in a 31-day August and all sets of dates are equally likely. Find the probability that no odd-numbered date is rainy.
problems.idea: All rainy dates must come from the 15 even-numbered dates.
steps: Choose the 10 rainy dates from the 15 even dates and divide by the total number of 10-date subsets.
problems.note: This calculation assumes the ten rainy dates are uniformly selected; knowing only the number of rainy days does not by itself specify a probability model.

problems.title: Two balls of the same colour
problems.question: A box has 8 red and 8 blue balls. Two are drawn together. Find the probability they have the same colour.
problems.idea: Count red-red and blue-blue pairs.
steps: The numerator is 56 and denominator 120.
Reduce the fraction.

problems.title: A minimum distance depending on one parameter
problems.question: Find the minimum distance between A=(t,2t+1,6) and B=(4,2,t).
problems.idea: Complete the square in the squared distance.
steps: Expand to get 6t²−24t+53=6(t−2)²+29.
The minimum squared distance is 29 at t=2.

problems.title: Three mutually perpendicular vectors
problems.question: Vectors (m,2,7),(6,n,3),(4,8,k) are pairwise perpendicular. Find m+n+k.
problems.idea: Set all three pairwise dot products to zero.
steps: The first gives n=−3m−21/2; the second k=−(4m+16)/7.
Substitute into the third to get −180m−468=0, so m=−13/5.
Then n=−27/10 and k=−4/5.
Their sum is −61/10.
